Routing Protocols in AS

Two sets routing protocols are used — (i) to determine routing paths within an AS;
(ii) others are used to interconnect a set of autonomous systems:

Interior Gateway Protocols (IGPs): Interior Gateway Protocols allow routers to exchange
information within an AS. Examples of these protocols are Open Short Path First (OSPF)
and Routing Information Protocol (RIP).

Exterior Gateway Protocols (EGPs): Exterior Gateway Protocols allow the exchange of
summary information between autonomous systems. An example of this type of routing

protocol is Border Gateway Protocol (BGP).
